name: Saturn from Voyager 2, September 1, 1981, 21:03 UTC
blurb: The ringed planet, about 120,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's narrow-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: A close view of part of Saturn, partly in shadow, from about 7 million kilometers away, 7 days after Voyager 2's closest approach to Saturn on August 26, 1981. Its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as a house.
